summary: Verified dynamic zig-zag layout of Alur Pendaftaran for N=0,1,2,3,4,5,10,11,12 stages and mobile 390px. Backend pytest (9/9 passed) at /app/backend/tests/test_registration_flow_zigzag.py exercises PUT /api/site/content with each stage count and re-GETs to confirm normalization/persistence. Frontend Playwright (real DOM against public preview URL): for each N, inspected computed CSS `order`, absolute x/y of each registration-flow-step-{i}, and class of registration-flow-arrow-{i}. Column derived from absolute x anchored to the 3-column grid (~92/513/935 at 1400px viewport). Results — all PASS: row/col of every step matches getDesktopPosition(index); arrow direction (right/left/down) matches getDesktopDirection(index); no arrow on last step. Key spec assertions confirmed: N=10 step10 col=2 row=3 and arrow 9->10 down; N=11 step11 col=1 (directly left of step10) and arrow 10->11 left; N=12 step12 col=0 row=3 and arrow 11->12 left. Trailing invisible placeholders (`hidden lg:block`) correctly force incomplete right-to-left rows into the right-most column. N=0 hides the section entirely (registration-flow-grid absent). Mobile 390px: horizontal overflow=0px, steps ordered 1..11 top-to-bottom, registration-flow-mobile-arrow-1..10 present, none on step 11. Original 11-stage production flow (first title 'Pembuatan Akun') fully restored via API after each test and at the end; verified via GET.
critical_code_review_comments: RegistrationFlow.jsx: getDesktopPosition/getDesktopDirection/getTrailingPlaceholderOrders are pure helpers with correct zig-zag math and are automatically responsive to steps.length changes from CMS. Verified at 1..12 lengths.

The invisible trailing placeholders (`hidden lg:block lg:order-[var(--desktop-order)]`) intentionally reserve cells so CSS grid `order` reflects true right-to-left placement on incomplete last rows. Without them, incomplete R->L rows collapse to the left. Do NOT remove.

Arrow logic uses SAME testid registration-flow-arrow-{index+1} for both side (right/left) and down variants but different classes (bottom-[-36px] vs -left-10/-right-10). Test detection uses className substring — acceptable but tightly coupled to Tailwind classes; consider a `data-arrow-dir` attribute for more robust automated testing.
PUT /api/site/content expects payload wrapped as {"content": {...}} (per SiteContentInput). This is undocumented in the review request but matches existing tests — no action needed.
seed_data_creation: None persisted. Every test set temporary flow via PUT and the fixture (backend) + finally block (frontend) restored the original 11-stage flow. Final GET confirmed first title = 'Pembuatan Akun'.
context_for_next_testing_agent: PUT /api/site/content requires body {"content": {"registration_flow": [...] }}. Public rendering testids: registration-flow-grid, registration-flow-step-{i}, registration-flow-arrow-{i} (down/left/right variants — distinguish by className: bottom-[-36px] => down, -left-10 => left, -right-10 => right), registration-flow-mobile-arrow-{i}. Trailing placeholders are `<div class='hidden lg:block lg:order-[var(--desktop-order)]'>` — treat them as expected non-step grid children when auditing layout. Column detection in tests should use absolute x-anchors of the 3-column grid, NOT relative rank among rendered steps (relative rank fails for incomplete right-to-left rows because placeholders are invisible but occupy grid cells).
